title: Due to DMA, Siri AI delayed in EU for iOS 27 and iPadOS 27
content:
UPDATE
                    
                    
                        June 8, 2026
                    
                    
                
            Due to DMA, Siri AI delayed in EU for iOS 27 and iPadOS 27
                
                
                    Siri AI will be available to EU users on macOS 27 and visionOS 27
                
            
        Apple today introduced Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri, powered by Apple Intelligence. Unfortunately, due to the Digital Markets Act (DMA), Apple will not be able to ship Siri AI in the European Union with the release of iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. Over the past several months, EU regulators did not accept any of Apple’s proposed solutions to bring Siri AI to the EU while safely supporting other virtual assistants.
                 
             
                 “We’re deeply disappointed that our EU users won’t have Siri AI on iPhone or iPad when we share our new software releases later this year,” said Craig Federighi, Apple’s senior vice president of Software Engineering. “Our hope is to eventually bring Siri AI to the EU, and we will continue to engage with EU regulators on a path forward. However, their refusal to engage constructively on solutions that preserve privacy and security means we do not currently have a timeline for Siri AI’s availability on iOS and iPadOS in the EU.”
                 
             
                 When iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 launch later this year, users in the EU1 will not have access to Siri AI and its advanced capabilities — including the new dedicated app to revisit conversations, an expanded Visual Intelligence experience, integrated tools for writing, Siri mode in Camera on iOS, and other Siri AI capabilities announced at WWDC26. Because Siri AI on watchOS 27 requires a paired iPhone with Siri AI, EU users will not have access to Siri AI on watchOS 27.
                 
             
                 EU users will be able to access Siri AI on macOS 27 and visionOS 27. Developers located in the EU will not be able to test or use the new Siri AI features for their apps on iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and watchOS 27.
                 
             
                 Siri AI is private by design and deeply integrated across Apple’s platforms using on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy and security of iPhone into the cloud. However, under EU regulators’ extreme interpretation of the DMA, Apple would have to give any virtual assistant direct access to users’ private data — and the ability to directly control other installed applications — as soon as Siri AI is made available in the EU, without the essential protections necessary to keep users and their data safe.
                 
             
                 According to EU regulators, the DMA requires Apple to give any AI system nearly unlimited access to a user’s device, as well as the ability to act on that access autonomously without a user’s ongoing visibility and control. That includes the ability to read and send messages, make purchases, access files, and execute actions across any app. Security researchers have already shown that AI systems can be hijacked to steal personal data — like passwords and photos — and to permanently alter files and account settings without a user’s consent. As AI systems gain more capabilities, these risks are quickly increasing in frequency and scope.
                 
             
                 Given the serious risks to users, Apple designed a solution called Trusted System Agent — an intermediary that would allow virtual assistants to safely access the same features and capabilities as Siri AI for devices in the EU. Apple also shared a plan to launch Siri AI in the EU while gradually rolling out this new solution over an 18-month period. The European Commission said no. In fact, the European Commission did not agree to any of Apple’s proposals.
                 
             
                 Apple will continue working to bring these features to the European Union as safely as possible. However, given the clear dangers to EU users and the regulators’ failure to acknowledge these risks, there is currently no timeline for Siri AI’s availability in the EU on iOS and iPadOS.

report.summary: Citing DMA rules it says endanger privacy, Apple withholds Siri AI from EU users on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, keeping it on macOS 27 and visionOS 27.
report.background: Apple's clash with the European Commission has been building since the Digital Markets Act took effect in 2022. The DMA designated Apple a gatekeeper and forced interoperability and choice-screen changes; Apple already delayed Apple Intelligence and iPhone Mirroring for EU users in 2024, then rolled some features out later. In 2025 the EU fined Apple roughly €500 million over anti-steering rules, and regulators opened consultations on how voice assistants and AI systems should interoperate with iOS. The core tension: Brussels wants any virtual assistant to reach device functions and data on equal footing with Apple's own, while Apple argues unsupervised agentic access creates hijacking and data-theft risks. With Siri AI announced at WWDC26, that stalemate now blocks Apple's flagship AI launch in its largest regulated market.
key_points: When iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 ship later this year, EU users will get no Siri AI: no conversation-history app, no expanded Visual Intelligence, writing tools or Siri mode in Camera.
macOS 27 and visionOS 27 are exempt and will offer Siri AI in the EU, but watchOS 27 needs a paired iPhone running Siri AI, so EU Apple Watch users lose it too.
EU-based developers cannot test or use Siri AI features on iOS 27, iPadOS 27 or watchOS 27, effectively excluding them from building on the new capabilities.
Apple proposed a 'Trusted System Agent' intermediary plus an 18-month gradual rollout so rival assistants could inherit Siri AI's access safely; the European Commission rejected every proposal.

Apple says regulators demand that any AI system get near-limitless, autonomous device access without ongoing user visibility or control, and warns security researchers have already shown such agents can be hijacked.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is the first major case where an AI assistant launch is gated by competition law rather than silicon or models, making 'regulatory availability' a product roadmap item. EU users lose Apple's most advanced assistant on phones and tablets, and face a two-tier Apple ecosystem where Mac and Vision Pro pull ahead of iPhone. EU developers lose early access to Siri AI APIs, ceding app-integration experimentation to US and Asian rivals. Rival assistants, including Google Gemini and OpenAI's offerings, may gain EU footing if Apple is forced to open access, but they would inherit the same security questions. Expect lobbying, possible infringement proceedings, and slower Apple AI adoption across the bloc's 450 million consumers.
report.tools: To follow the technical argument, read Apple's Private Cloud Compute security research and its virtual research environment, which underpin Siri AI's privacy claims. For on-device assistant experimentation, developers can try Apple's MLX, llama.cpp, Ollama and Home Assistant's open-source Assist pipeline, which is a practical reference for assistant interoperability. Apple's App Intents and Foundation Models documentation shows how third-party assistants integrate, and the Commission's DMA interoperability consultation pages track the regulatory track.
